worksheets.title: Earning Income, Commission, and Australian Taxation

fluency_questions.prompt: Find the unknown normal hourly rate $R$ or overtime hours worked:

parts.label: a
parts.question: A worker works $38$ normal hours, $6$ hours at time-and-a-half, and $4$ hours at double time, earning $\$1870$. Find $R$.

parts.label: b
parts.question: A worker at $\$32/\text{h}$ works $38$ normal hours, $4$ hours at time-and-a-half, and $x$ hours at double time to earn $\$1728$. Find $x$.

parts.label: c
parts.question: A nurse receives $\$6110$ for $4$ weeks' annual leave including $17.5\%$ leave loading. Find her normal hourly rate for a $38$-hour week (to the nearest cent).

parts.label: d
parts.question: A technician works $38$ normal hours at $\$R/\text{h}$ and $5$ hours at time-and-a-half, earning $\$1693.25$. Find $R$.

parts.label: a
parts.question: An agent earns a $\$750$ retainer plus $3.5\%$ commission on all sales, receiving $\$2290$ in a week. Find total sales.

parts.label: b
parts.question: A broker earns $2\%$ on the first $\$100\,000$ of sales and $4.5\%$ on sales above $\$100\,000$. If total commission is $\$5600$, find total sales.

parts.label: c
parts.question: A car dealer pays $\$600$ weekly retainer plus $r\%$ on sales above $\$15\,000$. If $\$55\,000$ in sales yields $\$1800$ pay, find $r$.

parts.label: d
parts.question: Salesperson A ($\$800 + 2.5\%$ of sales) and Salesperson B ($\$350 + 4\%$ of sales) earn the same pay on sales of $\$S$. Find $S$.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Total income tax plus $2\%$ Medicare levy on a taxable income of $\$155\,000$

parts.label: b
parts.question: Taxable income if income tax (excluding Medicare levy) is $\$14\,788$

parts.label: c
parts.question: Taxable income if total tax including $2\%$ Medicare levy is $\$12\,688$

parts.label: d
parts.question: Effective tax rate (income tax $\div$ taxable income as a percentage to $2$ d.p.) for a taxable income of $\$100\,000$

fluency_questions.prompt: Calculate the tax saving from each pre-tax salary sacrifice or work-related deduction:

parts.label: a
parts.question: A worker earning $\$78\,000$ claims $\$4200$ in deductions ($30\%$ marginal bracket plus $2\%$ Medicare levy)

parts.label: b
parts.question: A specialist earning $\$160\,000$ salary-sacrifices $\$10\,000$ into superannuation (taxed at $15\%$ in super instead of $37\% + 2\%$ personal tax)

parts.label: c
parts.question: A worker earning $\$48\,000$ claims $\$5000$ in deductions, crossing the $\$45\,000$ bracket boundary ($30\%$ above $\$45\,000$, $16\%$ below, plus $2\%$ Medicare)

parts.label: d
parts.question: Net fortnightly pay ($26$ fortnights/year) for a worker on $\$90\,000$ taxable income after income tax and $2\%$ Medicare levy

application_questions.question: A Sydney auctioneer charges a three-tier commission on residential sales: $3\%$ on the first $\$400\,000$, $2\%$ on the next $\$400\,000$ ($\$400\,001$ to $\$800\,000$), and $1.2\%$ on the remainder above $\$800\,000$. If the auctioneer receives $\$25\,400$ commission on a terrace house, what was the sale price?

An engineer in Perth has a gross salary of $\$142\,000$, earns $\$3500$ in bank interest, and claims $\$4500$ in tax deductions. Her employer withheld $\$38\,200$ in PAYG tax during the year. Using the $\$135\,001\text{--}\$190\,000$ bracket ($\$31\,288 + 37\%$ over $\$135\,000$) plus the $2\%$ Medicare levy, determine whether she receives a tax refund or owes a tax bill, and state the amount.
application_questions.answer: Refund of $\$1872$ (taxable income $\$141\,000$; income tax $\$33\,508 +$ Medicare $\$2820 = \$36\,328$ total liability)

application_questions.question: A paramedic in Victoria works a $38$-hour base week at $\$R/\text{h}$, plus $6$ hours at time-and-a-half and $3$ hours at double time. Her gross pay for the week is $\$2226$. Find her base hourly rate $R$.

After income tax ($\$4288 + 30\%$ over $\$45\,000$) and the $2\%$ Medicare levy are deducted, a Melbourne software developer takes home a net annual income of $\$70\,412$. Find her gross taxable income.

reasoning_questions.question: For a resident taxpayer in the $\$45\,001\text{--}\$135\,000$ bracket ($\text{Tax} = 4288 + 0.30(x - 45\,000)$), prove that the effective tax rate $E(x) = \dfrac{\text{Tax}}{x}$ is given by $E(x) = 0.30 - \dfrac{9212}{x}$, and explain why $E(x)$ approaches $30\%$ from below as $x$ increases within the bracket.
reasoning_questions.answer: $\text{Tax} = 4288 + 0.30x - 13\,500 = 0.30x - 9212$. Dividing by $x$ gives $E(x) = 0.30 - \dfrac{9212}{x}$. Since $\dfrac{9212}{x} > 0$, $E(x) < 0.30$, and as $x$ increases, $\dfrac{9212}{x}$ decreases, so $E(x)$ increases towards $0.30$.

reasoning_questions.question: When Australia's Stage 3 tax cuts reduced the $\$45\,001\text{--}\$120\,000$ marginal rate from $32.5\%$ to $30\%$ and lowered the $\$18\,201\text{--}\$45\,000$ rate from $19\%$ to $16\%$, how much annual tax was saved by a taxpayer earning $\$100\,000$?

worksheets.title: Simple Interest, Repayment Modelling, and Direct Proportion

fluency_questions.prompt: Solve each simple interest problem involving exact time intervals or combined accounts:

parts.label: a
parts.question: Find the principal $P$ that grows to $A = \$14\,280$ after $32\text{ months}$ at $7.125\%\text{ p.a.}$ simple interest.

parts.label: b
parts.question: An investment of $\$8000$ earns simple interest for $219\text{ days}$ ($1\text{ year} = 365\text{ days}$), growing to $\$8312$. Find the annual interest rate.

parts.label: c
parts.question: How many years does it take for any principal $P$ to triple ($A = 3P$) at $8\%\text{ p.a.}$ simple interest?

parts.label: d
parts.question: A sum of $\$20\,000$ is split between Account A ($4.5\%\text{ p.a.}$) and Account B ($6.5\%\text{ p.a.}$). If the total annual interest is $\$1140$, how much was invested in Account B?

fluency_questions.prompt: For each hire-purchase agreement, calculate (i) the flat rate $r_f$ (% p.a.) and (ii) the approximate effective interest rate $r_e = \dfrac{2n}{n+1} r_f$ where $n$ is the number of monthly instalments:

parts.label: a
parts.question: Balance owing $\$3000$ repaid over $n = 24$ months at $\$145/\text{month}$

parts.label: b
parts.question: Balance owing $\$6000$ repaid over $n = 35$ months at $\$200/\text{month}$

parts.label: c
parts.question: Cash price $\$4500$, $20\%$ deposit, $n = 15$ monthly payments of $\$264$

parts.label: d
parts.question: Find the flat rate $r_f$ if a $23$-month loan has an effective rate $r_e = 11.5\%\text{ p.a.}$

parts.label: a
parts.question: $y \propto x$ and $y = 45$ when $x = 12$. Find $y$ when $x = 32$.

parts.label: b
parts.question: $P$ is directly proportional to $Q$, and increasing $Q$ by $6$ increases $P$ by $27$. Find the constant of proportionality $k$ and $P$ when $Q = 14$.

parts.label: c
parts.question: If $y \propto x$ and $x$ is increased by $35\%$, by what percentage does $y$ increase?

parts.label: d
parts.question: Given $y \propto x^2$ (direct variation with the square) and $y = 54$ when $x = 3$, find $y$ when $x = 5$.

fluency_questions.prompt: Rearrange each financial or proportionality formula for the specified variable:

parts.label: a
parts.question: Make $t$ the subject of $A = P(1 + rt)$

parts.label: b
parts.question: Make $r$ the subject of $A = P(1 + rt)$

parts.label: c
parts.question: Make $n$ the subject of $R = \dfrac{2n}{n+1} r$

parts.label: d
parts.question: Make $D$ (deposit) the subject of $M = \dfrac{(C - D)(1 + rt)}{12t}$

application_questions.question: A farmer in the Riverina invests a total of $\$50\,000$ across two simple interest bonds: Bond X pays $4.8\%\text{ p.a.}$ and Bond Y pays $6.0\%\text{ p.a.}$. After $2.5\text{ years}$, the combined interest from both bonds is $\$6900$. How much was invested in each bond?

A solar battery system in Brisbane has a cash price of $\$9000$. A homeowner pays a $10\%$ deposit and repays the balance over $3$ years in equal monthly instalments of $\$268.20$. Find (a) the flat annual simple interest rate $r_f$ and (b) the approximate effective interest rate $r_e = \dfrac{2n}{n+1} r_f$ to $2$ decimal places.

The mass $M\text{ g}$ of a uniform copper wire is directly proportional to its length $L\text{ m}$, while its electrical resistance $R\;\Omega$ is also directly proportional to $L$. A $15\text{ m}$ coil of wire has mass $420\text{ g}$ and resistance $0.36\;\Omega$. Express $R$ directly in terms of $M$, and find the resistance of a coil of mass $1.05\text{ kg}$.

An investor places $\$P$ at $5\%\text{ p.a.}$ simple interest for $4$ years, then immediately reinvests the entire accumulated amount $A_1$ into a new account paying $6\%\text{ p.a.}$ simple interest for $5$ years. If the final amount is $\$19\,500$, find the original principal $P$.

reasoning_questions.question: Explain why a flat interest rate $r_f$ on a monthly hire-purchase loan understates the true cost of borrowing, and show using $r_e = \dfrac{2n}{n+1} r_f$ that as the number of months $n$ becomes large, the effective interest rate is nearly double the flat rate.
reasoning_questions.answer: Under flat-rate interest, interest is charged on the full initial balance for the entire term even though monthly repayments steadily reduce the principal owed (on average, only about half the principal is owed over the term). As $n$ grows large, $\dfrac{2n}{n+1} = \dfrac{2}{1 + 1/n} \to 2$, so $r_e \approx 2r_f$.

reasoning_questions.question: Prove that if $y$ is directly proportional to $x$ ($y = k_1 x$) and $z$ is directly proportional to $y$ ($z = k_2 y$), then $z$ is directly proportional to $x$ and state its constant of proportionality.
reasoning_questions.answer: Substituting $y = k_1 x$ into $z = k_2 y$ gives $z = k_2(k_1 x) = (k_1 k_2)x$. Since $k_1 k_2$ is a constant, $z \propto x$ with constant of proportionality $k = k_1 k_2$.
